purpose: Reusable identities and attributes shared across Sacred Art stories

people.name: The Virgin Mary
people.summary: Jesus' mother. In the Annunciation, Gabriel announces that she will bear Jesus.
clues: Usually the woman receiving a message from an angel in Annunciation scenes
Often wears blue, though her clothing varies
Often shown with a book, a lectern, a lily nearby, or an enclosed garden
people.care: A blue robe or a book alone does not prove that a woman is Mary. Identify her role in the story and surrounding figures.

people.name: Saint Gabriel the Archangel
people.summary: God's messenger who announces to Mary that she will bear Jesus.
clues: Winged messenger addressing Mary
Often carries lilies, an olive branch, a staff or a scroll with a greeting
May kneel, bow, point toward heaven or approach Mary
people.care: Wings alone show that someone is an angel, not necessarily Gabriel. Use the scene and his message to identify him.

people.name: Saint Ansanus
people.summary: An early Christian martyr and patron of Siena. He is included in Simone Martini and Lippo Memmi's Annunciation because the altarpiece was made for his altar.
clues: A standing young male martyr on the far left of the altarpiece
A banner showing Siena's traditional black-and-white colors
A martyr's palm
people.care: A banner or palm by itself is not unique to Ansanus. The Siena altar's dedication and the painting's history provide important supporting evidence.
artworks: Simone Martini and Lippo Memmi's Annunciation

people.name: Saint Joseph
people.summary: Mary's husband, from the family of David, and Jesus' earthly guardian.
clues: Shown close to Mary and the infant Jesus in Nativity scenes
Often appears as an older bearded man, sometimes standing apart or holding a staff
In other artworks may hold a lily, tools associated with carpentry, or the Christ Child
people.care: Age, beard or staff is not enough on its own. Identify the Holy Family scene and Joseph's relationship to Mary and Jesus.

people.name: Saint Anne
people.summary: Mary's mother according to Christian tradition.
clues: Often shown as an older woman teaching the young Mary to read
May appear with Mary and the infant Jesus to show three generations
Often accompanied by a book in teaching scenes
people.care: An older woman near Mary is not automatically Anne. The traditional family relationship, a teaching scene or a documented painting context matters.

people.name: Saint Catherine of Alexandria
people.summary: A learned Christian martyr of royal status in later tradition.
clues: Spiked wheel associated with her martyrdom legend
Crown denoting the princess of tradition
Sometimes a sword or a book
people.care: Fra Angelico's Nativity shows her crown, but a wheel may not appear. Different paintings show different attributes.

people.name: Saint Peter Martyr (Peter of Verona)
people.summary: A thirteenth-century Dominican preacher and martyr.
clues: Black-and-white Dominican habit
A head wound or blade associated with martyrdom
Sometimes a martyr's palm
people.care: Do not confuse him with Saint Peter the Apostle, who is often shown with keys. Look for Dominican clothing and the martyr's injury.

people.name: Saint Thomas the Apostle
people.summary: An apostle of Jesus, shown as a patron saint of Tommaso Portinari.
clues: Spear associated with traditions about his martyrdom
Can appear with a donor named Thomas or Tommaso
Sometimes shown touching Jesus' wounds in Resurrection scenes
people.care: Do not assume everyone holding a spear is Thomas. Combine the attribute, name saint and surrounding context.

people.name: Saint Anthony the Abbot
people.summary: An Egyptian desert hermit of the third and fourth centuries.
clues: T-shaped tau staff or crutch
Bell and sometimes a pig
Often an elderly monk or hermit
people.care: Not Saint Anthony of Padua. A pig, bell or tau staff together provide stronger clues than the name Anthony alone.

people.name: Saint Anthony of Padua
people.summary: A thirteenth-century Franciscan friar, a different person from Anthony the Abbot.
clues: Young Franciscan friar's habit
Lily, book or the Christ Child
people.care: His objects differ from the bell, tau staff and pig often associated with Anthony the Abbot.

people.name: Saint Margaret of Antioch
people.summary: A martyr associated with a dragon in her legend.
clues: Dragon beneath or beside her
Often carrying a cross or palm
people.care: Her identity in the Portinari Triptych is established. Do not assume that the disputed female saint in Simone Martini's Annunciation is Margaret.

people.name: Saint Mary Magdalene
people.summary: A follower of Jesus, traditionally associated with anointing and a jar of ointment.
clues: Ointment or perfume jar
Sometimes loose long hair or rich garments
people.care: A jar is a conventional symbol, not a guaranteed unique label. Check the scene and other figures.

people.name: Saint John the Baptist
people.summary: The prophet who prepared the way for Jesus and baptized him in the Jordan.
clues: Camel-hair clothing or rough wilderness garments
Reed cross-staff, lamb or scroll referring to the Lamb of God
May appear beside a river or in a baptism scene
people.care: Not Saint John the Evangelist. In a scene depicting the Baptism of Jesus, the person baptizing Jesus is John the Baptist.

people.name: Saint John the Evangelist
people.summary: Traditionally associated with the fourth Gospel and the eagle symbol.
clues: Book or writing materials
An eagle used as the Evangelist symbol
Sometimes a youthful apostle with a cup or chalice
people.care: Not John the Baptist. Book and eagle are stronger clues than simply being a young man.

people.name: Isaiah
people.summary: An Old Testament prophet whose words Christians connect with the coming of Jesus.
clues: Often holds a scroll or book, sometimes with a quotation from Isaiah
In Duccio's Nativity the left scroll quotes Isaiah 7:14
people.care: Scrolls are common to prophets, so the biblical quotation is the strongest identifying clue in Duccio's painting.

people.name: Ezekiel
people.summary: An Old Testament prophet whose book includes the image of a closed gate, later interpreted symbolically by Christians.
clues: Often holds a scroll or book
In Duccio's Nativity the right scroll refers to Ezekiel 44:2
people.care: The scroll's text matters more than which side of the panel he stands on.
